requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: The select case statement IS an alternative syntactic form of the if-else statement.
requirements.original: The select case statement is an alternative syntactic form of the if-else statement.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: The select case statement has the syntax `select` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" followed by one or more list branches `case` "(" {TemplateInstance [","]} ")" StatementBlock, an optional else branch `case else` StatementBlock, and a closing "}".
requirements.original:
select "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" 
     { case "(" { TemplateInstance[","] } ")" StatementBlock }+
     [ case else StatementBlock ]
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: The select case statement IS an alternative to nested if-else statements when comparing a value to one or several other values.
requirements.original: The select case statement is an alternative to using if .. else `if .. else statements when comparing a value to` one or several other values.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: A select case statement IS composed of a header part and one or more branches.
requirements.original: The statement contains a header part and one or more branches.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: An execution of a select case statement SHALL NOT execute more than one of its branches.
requirements.original: Never more than one of the branches is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:header-part
requirements.canonical: The header part of a select case statement SHALL contain an expression.
requirements.original: In the header part of the select case statement an expression shall be given.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The expression in the header part of a select case statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: The expression may be preceded by an _init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a select case statement IS executed before the header expression is evaluated.
requirements.original: The expression may be preceded by an _init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a select case statement SHALL be limited to the select case statement.
requirements.original: The scope of_ variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the select case statement.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.canonical: A list branch of a select case statement IS the `case` keyword followed by a list of one or more template instances and a statement block.
requirements.original: Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the BNF name 'templateInstance' instead of the term 'template instance'.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: The last branch of a select case statement MAY be an else branch consisting of the `case` keyword followed by the `else` keyword and a statement block.
requirements.original: Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: An else branch SHALL only appear as the last branch of a select case statement.
requirements.original: Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: Every template instance in a list branch of a select case statement SHALL be of a type compatible with the type of the header expression.
requirements.original: All templateInstance in all list branches shall be of a type compatible with the type of the expression in the header.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the BNF name 'templateInstance' instead of the term 'template instance'.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.canonical: A list branch of a select case statement IS selected, and its statement block executed, only if at least one of its template instances matches the value of the header expression.
requirements.original: A list branch is selected and the statement block of the selected branch is executed only, if any of the templateInstance matches the value of the expression in the header of the statement.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: the statement block of the selected branch is executed without jumping out by a goto statement
requirements.canonical: When the statement block of the selected branch has been executed without jumping out by a goto statement, execution SHALL continue with the statement following the select case statement.
requirements.original: On executing the statement block of the selected branch (i.e. not jumping out by a goto statement), execution continues with the statement following the select case statement.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: no textually preceding branch has been selected
requirements.canonical: The statement block of an else branch IS executed if no branch textually preceding the else branch has been selected.
requirements.original: The statement block of an else branch is always executed if no other branch textually preceding the else branch has been selected.

requirements.subject: ent:branch
requirements.canonical: The branches of a select case statement ARE evaluated in their textual order.
requirements.original: Branches are evaluated in their textual order.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: no template instance matches and there is no else branch
requirements.canonical: If none of the template instances matches the value of the header expression and the select case statement contains no else branch, execution continues after the select case statement without executing any branch.
requirements.original: If none of the templateInstance-s matches the value of the expression in the header and the statement contains no else branch, execution continues without executing any of the select case branches.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool CANNOT in general decide whether the template instances of a select case statement overlap.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: In general, it cannot be decided if templateInstances overlap or not.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The template instances used in the branches of a select case statement SHOULD NOT overlap.
requirements.original: However, it is advised to use in the branches templateInstances that don't overlap.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the template instances do not overlap
requirements.canonical: When the template instances of a select case statement do not overlap, a TTCN-3 tool CAN provide better runtime performance.
requirements.original: In such situations tools might provide better runtime performance.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The handling of non-overlapping template instances in a select case statement IS tool-specific.
requirements.original: The handling however is tool-specific.

ambiguity.issue: 'The handling' has no clear referent; chosen reading: the performance optimisation for non-overlapping template instances is tool-specific.
readings: The optimisation of select case statements with non-overlapping template instances IS tool-specific.
The handling of overlapping template instances in a select case statement IS tool-specific.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: the template instances of more than one branch match
requirements.canonical: When more than one branch of a select case statement could be selected because the template instances overlap, the textually first branch IS selected.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When more than one branch could be selected (the templateInstances overlap) the textually first will be selected.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: Overlapping template instances SHOULD NOT be used in the branches of a select case statement.
requirements.original: For this reason overlapping is discouraged, handling however is tool-specific.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The handling of overlapping template instances in a select case statement IS tool-specific.
requirements.original: For this reason overlapping is discouraged, handling however is tool-specific.

ambiguity.issue: Contradicts the preceding sentence of NOTE 2, which states that the textually first branch is selected; chosen reading: only tool optimisation is tool-specific.
readings: Selection of the textually first matching branch IS mandated; only the internal optimisation IS tool-specific.
Which branch IS selected for overlapping template instances IS tool-specific.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the header of a select case statement and every case template instance SHALL be type compatible.
requirements.original: a) The select _SingleExpression and the case TemplateInstance-s shall be type compatible._

requirements.subject: ent:branch
requirements.condition: all template instances can be evaluated at compile time to specific values or value ranges
requirements.canonical: If all template instances of all branches of a select case statement can be statically evaluated at compile time to specific values or value ranges, two branches SHALL NOT match the same value.
requirements.original: b) When all templateInstances of all branches can be statically evaluated in compile time to specific values or value ranges no two branches shall match the same value.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: The select union statement IS a special form of the select statement for values of union types or anytype.
requirements.original: To allow easier usage of the select statement for values of union types or anytype, a special form of the select statement exists.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: The select union statement has the syntax `select union` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" followed by one or more branches `case` "(" ({Identifier [","]} | {TypeIdentifier [","]}) ")" StatementBlock, an optional `case else` StatementBlock, and a closing "}".
requirements.original:
select union "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" 
     { case "(" ({ Identifier [","] } | { TypeIdentifier [","] }) ")" StatementBlock }+
     [ case else StatementBlock ]
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: A select union statement IS composed of a header part and one or more branches.
requirements.original: The statement contains a header part and one or more branches.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: An execution of a select union statement SHALL NOT execute more than one of its branches.
requirements.original: Never more than one of the branches is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:header-part
requirements.canonical: The header part of a select union statement SHALL contain a template instance of a union type or of anytype.
requirements.original: In the header part of the select union statement a template instance of union type or anytype shall be given.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The expression in the header of a select union statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: The expression in the header may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a select union statement IS executed before the header expression is evaluated.
requirements.original: The expression in the header may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a select union statement SHALL be limited to the select union statement.
requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the select union statement.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has a union type
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has a union type, each list branch SHALL start with the `case` keyword followed by one or more identifiers of alternatives (fields) of the union type.
requirements.original: If the template instance has a union type, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more identifiers of the alternatives (fields) of the union type (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has a union type
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has a union type, the last branch MAY be an else branch consisting of `case else` and a statement block.
requirements.original: If the template instance has a union type, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more identifiers of the alternatives (fields) of the union type (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has type anytype
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has type anytype, each list branch SHALL start with the `case` keyword followed by one or more type names.
requirements.original: If the template instance has type anytype, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more type names (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has type anytype
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has type anytype, the last branch MAY be an else branch consisting of `case else` and a statement block.
requirements.original: If the template instance has type anytype, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more type names (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.canonical: The statement block of the list branch containing the identifier or type identifier of the chosen alternative IS executed.
requirements.original: The StatementBlock of the list branch containing the identifier or type identifier of the chosen alternative is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: no case exists for the chosen alternative and an else branch is present
requirements.canonical: If no case exists for the chosen alternative and an else branch is present, the statement block of the else branch IS executed.
requirements.original: If no case exists for the chosen alternative, the StatementBlock of the else branch, if it is present, is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.condition: no case exists for the chosen alternative and no else branch is present
requirements.canonical: If no case exists for the chosen alternative and no else branch is present, the select union statement HAS no effect.
requirements.original: Otherwise, the select union statement has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be of a union type or anytype.
requirements.original: a) The SingleExpression in the header of the select union statement shall be of a union type.

ambiguity.issue: Restriction a) only mentions union types, while the semantic description and the example also allow anytype; chosen reading: anytype is included.
readings: The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be of a union type or anytype.
The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be of a union type only.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: It shall be at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:case-keyword
requirements.canonical: Every Identifier in a case of a select union statement SHALL be the identifier of an alternative of the union type of the header template instance.
requirements.original: b) Every Identifier in a case of the select union statement shall be an identifier of an alternative of the union type of the template instance given to the statement's header.

requirements.subject: ent:case-keyword
requirements.canonical: Two cases of a select union statement SHALL NOT have the same case Identifier or TypeIdentifier.
requirements.original: c) No two cases in a select union statement shall have the same case Identifier or TypeIdentifier.

non_requirement.reason: introduces the restriction list; refers to general static rules in clause 5 and table 16
